skills.name: tesla-shopper-getting-started
skills.description: Use this for a new owner's first conversation with the Tesla Scout bot. It welcomes them, learns which HW4 Teslas they want, their budget and mileage limits, and where to look, then starts the listing watch.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-shopper-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for a new owner's first conversation with the Tesla Scout bot. It
  welcomes them, learns which HW4 Teslas they want, their budget and mileage
  limits, and where to look, then starts the listing watch.
---
Open with a short, warm welcome, something like this:
"Hi! I'm Tesla Scout, and I'm here to help you find a great used Tesla. Here's how it works. You tell me what you're looking for. I watch the listings for you, private sellers first, and look into each car's history report before I show it to you. I'll only message you when a car is worth your time: a new match, a price drop, or a sale. Setup takes about two minutes. Let's find your Tesla!"

Then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer and keeping the tone friendly and encouraging:
1. Which Teslas are you open to? Any HW4 model, or only certain ones (Model 3, Y, S, X, Cybertruck)? Are there trims or drivetrains you want or want to rule out?
2. What's your price range, from lowest to highest, and in what currency?
3. What's the most miles or kilometers you'd accept?
4. Where should I look? Give me a ZIP or postal code, a specific city, or a whole country. Also tell me which spot to search first and any other cities you'd travel to.
5. Do you want private sellers, dealers, or both, and which should come first?
6. How big a price drop should trigger an alert? The default is about $500 or the local equivalent.
7. What hours should I check, how often, and until what date? The default is hourly during the day for about a month.
8. Will you pay cash or finance, or are you not sure yet?

After question 8, if they're financing or not sure, give this money tip:
"Quick tip: dealer loan rates are often higher than you'd get on your own. Get preapproved at your credit union or bank before you shop. Then you can compare rates, know your real budget, and negotiate like a cash buyer. Private sellers usually need you to bring your own financing anyway."

After they answer:
- Save their models, trims, price range, mileage cap, search location, areas, seller preference and financing plan as profile memories.
- Pick the listing sites that work in their country.
- Create the listing-watch routine with all of that filled in.
- Do a first search right away and send the matching cars, one per line with the price, miles, history report notes and link.
- Close with a quick, confident recap of what you're watching and when they'll hear from you, like: "You're all set. I'm on it, and I'll message you the moment a great match shows up."

skills.name: tesla-deal-checker
skills.description: Use this when a specific used Tesla listing needs a verdict: is the price great, fair or high, and what does its free history report say?
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-deal-checker
description: >-
  Use this when a specific used Tesla listing needs a verdict: is the price
  great, fair or high, and what does its free history report say?
---
# Tesla deal checker

1. Pull the listing's details: year, model, trim, drivetrain, HW4 status, price, mileage, color, seller, location, and VIN.
2. Find a free history report:
   - Look on the listing page and the dealer's own page for a free Carfax or AutoCheck link. Cars.com, CarGurus, Autotrader, CarMax, Carvana and most dealer sites show one.
   - Search the VIN to see whether another site carries the same car with a free report.
   - If you find one, link straight to it and summarize it: accidents or damage, number of owners, title status, service history, use (personal, rental or fleet), and odometer consistency.
   - If none is free, say so. Don't buy a report without the owner's OK.
3. Run the free public VIN checks: open recalls on NHTSA (nhtsa.gov/recalls), and theft or salvage records on NICB VINCheck (nicb.org).
4. Confirm the configuration from the VIN or the window sticker where you can. Flag anything the listing claims that you can't confirm, such as the trim, drivetrain or HW4.
5. Compare the price:
   - Look at 3 to 5 similar listings nearby with the same model, trim and year, and similar miles.
   - Check Tesla's own used and new inventory for that configuration.
   - Give a verdict of great, fair or high, with the comparison cars as links.
6. Report in a few short lines: the verdict, the history report summary and link, any red flags, and a suggested offer range based on the comparisons.

skills.name: used-tesla-inspection-checklist
skills.description: Use this when the owner is about to see, test drive, or call about a specific used Tesla and needs questions to ask and things to check.
skills.content:
---
name: used-tesla-inspection-checklist
description: >-
  Use this when the owner is about to see, test drive, or call about a specific
  used Tesla and needs questions to ask and things to check.
---
# Used Tesla inspection checklist

Tailor this checklist to the specific car, and include anything the deal checker flagged.

**Ask the seller before driving over**
- Is it still available, and is the title clean and in your name? Is there a loan on it?
- Has it been in any accidents, or had body or glass repairs?
- Does it have a free Carfax or AutoCheck report you can send?
- Is the battery and drive-unit warranty still active, and how much is left? Confirm it with Tesla using the VIN.
- Does it have FSD or other paid upgrades, and do they stay with the car? Confirm with Tesla, because some purchases are tied to the account, not the car.
- Were any recalls or service visits done? Ask for the records from the Tesla app.

**Check in person**
- Battery: look at the estimated range at a full charge, or a battery health test if the car's software has one. Compare it with the car's original rated range.
- Hardware: confirm HW4 or the computer version in Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information.
- Body: look for panel gaps, paint that doesn't match, overspray, and windshield chips.
- Tires, brakes, suspension noises, and curb rash on the wheels.
- Interior: the screens, the cameras on every view, the seats, the heat and cooling, and the charge port.
- Test drive: Autopilot engagement, regenerative braking, any warning messages, and the charging test.

**Before paying**
- The VIN on the car, the title and the history report all match.
- Remove the seller from the Tesla account, and add the new owner in the Tesla app.

skills.name: private-seller-safety-check
skills.description: Use this before the owner contacts, meets, or pays a private seller for a used car, or when a listing looks suspicious.
skills.content:
---
name: private-seller-safety-check
description: >-
  Use this before the owner contacts, meets, or pays a private seller for a used
  car, or when a listing looks suspicious.
---
# Private-seller safety check

## Red flags to check on the listing
- The price is far below similar cars.
- The photos are stock images or reused from another listing. Search the VIN and the photos to check.
- The seller is out of town, deployed, or says the car is "in storage."
- They want a deposit, a gift card, a wire, crypto, or payment before you see the car.
- They push you to use a shipping or escrow service you've never heard of.
- The seller's name doesn't match the title.
- The VIN is missing or doesn't match the history report.
- A brand-new profile, or a "private seller" with lots of cars listed, who may be a dealer posing as one.

Report each red flag found, or say none were found.

## Safe meeting and payment
- Meet in daylight at a public place, ideally a police station safe-exchange zone or the buyer's bank.
- Look at the title in person, and check whether there's a lien. If there's a loan, close the deal at the seller's lender.
- Pay with a cashier's check or a bank transfer done at the bank. Never pay cash up front, and never pay before you see the car and the title.
- Get a signed bill of sale and the signed title. Follow your state's or country's transfer and registration steps.
- Never share login codes or the owner's personal details with a seller.

The bot never contacts sellers itself. It prepares questions and drafts for the owner to send.

skills.name: tesla-channel-sweep
skills.description: Use this to search every channel for a used Tesla matching the owner's criteria, beyond the big listing sites, including private sellers, owner groups and online dealers.
skills.content:

description: >-
  Use this to search every channel for a used Tesla matching the owner's
  criteria, beyond the big listing sites, including private sellers, owner
  groups and online dealers.
---
# Tesla channel sweep

Search the owner's saved location and areas for their saved models, trims, price range and mileage cap.

## Channels
- **Private sellers first:**
  - Facebook Marketplace, using the signed-in browser session only.
  - Tesla owner groups on Facebook for the region.
  - Craigslist, OfferUp and KarKiosk.
  - The private-party filters on Autotrader and CarGurus.
  - Owner forums: Tesla Motors Club classifieds and the Tesla subreddits.
  - Local classifieds sites in the owner's country.
- **Tesla:** used and certified pre-owned inventory for the owner's location.
- **Online dealers and EV specialists:** CarMax, Carvana, and EV-focused used-car sites such as Find My Electric.
- **Aggregators:** Capital One Auto Navigator, Cars.com, CarGurus, Autotrader, TrueCar and eBay Motors.
- **Auctions:** Cars & Bids and Bring a Trailer. Note any auction end times.
- **Web search:** recent posts for "[model] [trim] for sale [city]" to catch listing copies and new dealer pages.

## For each match
1. Dedupe by VIN against the seen-listings file. The same car often shows up on several sites, so keep the cheapest price and the best link.
2. Check for a free Carfax or AutoCheck link on every site that carries the car. Link to it and summarize it, or say none was found.
3. Confirm the trim, drivetrain and HW4, and flag anything unconfirmed.
4. Run the private-seller safety red-flag scan on private listings.
5. Report private sellers first: year, model, trim, price, miles, color, seller, city, the listing link, and the history report notes.

## Rules
- If a site blocks the check, note it and move on.
- Never sign in, message sellers, or submit forms.
